aiken/merkle_patricia_forestry/Neighbor.title: Neighbor
aiken/merkle_patricia_forestry/Neighbor.description: since | 1.0.0 --- | --- A neighbor node used in a proof. See [Proof](#Proof) for details.

aiken/merkle_patricia_forestry/ProofStep.title: ProofStep
aiken/merkle_patricia_forestry/ProofStep.description: since | 1.0.0 --- | --- We distinguish three kind of proof steps: Branch, Fork and Leaf. Each step contains a `skip` value which corresponds to the length of the common prefix at that particular level. The details of each level is documented [in the wiki :: Proof Format](https://github.com/aiken-lang/merkle-patricia-forestry/wiki/Proof-format).

cardano/transaction/OutputReference.title: OutputReference
cardano/transaction/OutputReference.description:
An `OutputReference` is a unique reference to an output on-chain. The `output_index`
 corresponds to the position in the output list of the transaction (identified by its id)
 that produced that output

types/denylist/MintRedeemer.title: MintRedeemer
types/denylist/MintRedeemer.description:
Mint redeemer. Add/Remove are gated by a power user holding `is_admin`;
 Deinit by the GS admin credential; Init is nonce-gated. Each gated action
 carries a reference-input index to the GS UTxO. Add/Remove additionally
 carry `power_user_node_ref_input_index`, pointing at the power-user linked-
 list node (a reference input) whose `is_admin` flag + signature authorise
 the sanction; the power-user list policy id is read from the GS datum.

types/denylist/SpendRedeemer.title: SpendRedeemer
types/denylist/SpendRedeemer.description:
Spend redeemer. Only `StateTransition` — all mutation logic delegates to
 the mint validator. No `ModifyUser` analogue: presence IS the state, there
 is nothing to toggle within a node.

types/global_state/GlobalStateDatum.title: GlobalStateDatum
types/global_state/GlobalStateDatum.description:
GlobalState datum — authenticated by the single global_state NFT.

 INVARIANT: `transfers_paused` MUST remain at field index 0. The fast
 pause-read via `is_paused` below relies on `unconstr_fields` + `head_list`
 to pull the first field without deserialising the whole datum. Reshuffling
 fields breaks that optimisation.

fields.title: member_root_hash
fields.description: Root hash of the MPF membership tree (32 bytes); empty = no members yet

types/global_state/GlobalStateSpendActio.title: GlobalStateSpendAction
types/global_state/GlobalStateSpendActio.description:
Spend actions on the global_state UTxO. Admin-gated actions read the
 current admin credential hash from the input datum — which means the
 compile-time owner parameter is gone. Rotation happens via `RotateAdmin`
 with dual-signature (old + new admin).

anyOf.title: RotateMintingScript
anyOf.description:
Swaps which script's withdraw-0 minting_logic_script.ak (the permanent
 CIP-113 proxy) delegates mint/burn authorisation to. Admin-signed only
 — deliberately single-signature, unlike RotateAdmin/dual-sig patterns
 elsewhere: the outgoing authority's own consent is not required, since
 an authority being replaced (e.g. because it is buggy or compromised)
 is exactly the scenario this action needs to handle even when that
 script itself can no longer be trusted to co-sign.

anyOf.title: LockUpgrades
anyOf.description:
ONE-WAY upgrade lock — see `upgrades_locked`. Admin-signed, and
 deliberately not reversible: a lock an admin can lift is not a
 commitment. Rejected if already locked, so the action is not a silent
 no-op.

anyOf.title: DeactivateContract
anyOf.description:
One-way decommissioning switch. Sets `deactivated = True`. Requires the
 contract to already be paused and the admin to sign. Irreversible: no
 action sets it back to False, and once set every spend of the
 global_state UTxO is rejected (see the terminal guard in the spend
 validator), which permanently freezes transfers (stays paused) and
 mint/burn (MintSecurity can no longer run).

types/kyc_proof/AttestationProof.title: AttestationProof
types/kyc_proof/AttestationProof.description:
A KYC proof is a short-lived Ed25519 signature from a trusted issuer
 attesting that a specific user is KYC'd for a specific security token on a
 specific network, valid until a specific moment.

 Payload layout (exactly 66 bytes, big-endian ordering where applicable):

     Bytes  0 – 27  : user_pkh          (28)  — binds proof to a specific sender
     Byte      28   : user_kyc_tier     (1)   — 0x00 invalid; 0x01 User;
                                                0x02 Institutional; 0x03 vLEI
     Bytes 29 – 36  : valid_until_ms    (8)   — POSIX ms, big-endian
     Bytes 37 – 64  : security_policy_id(28)  — binds to a specific token
     Byte      65   : network_id        (1)   — 0x00 preview; 0x01 preprod;
                                                0x02 mainnet; 0x03 yaci

 Signature: 64-byte raw Ed25519 over the payload.
 Issuer vkey: 32-byte raw Ed25519 vkey — directly indexes
   `GlobalStateDatum.trusted_entity_vkeys`.

types/minting_authority/MintingAuthority.title: MintingAuthorityWithdrawRedeemer
types/minting_authority/MintingAuthority.description:
Withdraw redeemer for validators/minting_authority.ak — the swappable
 minting authority named by `GlobalStateDatum.minting_script_credential_
 hash` (admin-rotatable via `RotateMintingScript`).

 minting_logic_script.ak (the permanent, CIP-113-registered proxy) requires
 this validator's withdraw-0 to be present for any transaction that moves
 the security token's supply, but hands this validator NOTHING
 pre-verified — this redeemer carries everything needed to decide, and
 every input is independently re-resolved and re-checked here. The two
 variants differ only in where this token's registry node can be found.

anyOf.title: MintBurn
anyOf.description:
Steady state: the registry node already exists as a UTxO and is
 supplied as a reference input.

fields.title: registry_node_ref_input_index
fields.description:
Index into `self.reference_inputs` — the CIP-113 registry node for
 THIS token. Independently re-resolved and re-verified here (against
 this deployment's known, permanent proxy hash — NOT this script's own
 hash, since the registry node names the proxy) rather than trusted
 from the proxy: without this, a redeemer could name an unrelated
 (decoy) issuance policy, making every check below vacuous while a
 DIFFERENT, real mint under the genuine policy proceeds unchecked.

fields.title: global_state_input_index
fields.description:
Index into `self.inputs` — the same GlobalState UTxO the proxy
 resolves (shared, transaction-wide data; a wrong index just fails the
 NFT check).

fields.title: minted_amount
fields.description: Amount minted (signed: positive for mint, negative for burn).

fields.title: destination_actions
fields.description:
One action per unique destination stake credential among outputs
 carrying the security token. Only consulted when `minted_amount > 0`
 (burns have no destinations); ordered to match the aggregated
 unique-destinations order.

anyOf.title: RegisterMint
anyOf.description:
The first mint, carried by the CIP-113 registration that creates this
 token's registry node. Identical authorisation to `MintBurn` — the node
 is simply reached through `self.outputs`, because at insert time it is
 an output of this very transaction rather than a pre-existing UTxO.

 The proxy still owns the registration's own structural invariants (that
 the node names it, forbids unfracking, and pins this deployment's
 GlobalState) and the admin gate on registering at all; this variant
 authorises only the mint that rides along with it.

fields.title: registry_node_output_index
fields.description:
Index into `self.outputs` — the registry node being created. An
 insert emits TWO registry-node outputs (the new node and the
 re-emitted covering node), so the index alone does not identify ours;
 the identity assertion against the proxy's hash disambiguates.

fields.title: global_state_input_index
fields.description:
Index into `self.inputs` — GlobalState, SPENT so its `MintSecurity`
 branch decrements and enforces `mintable_amount`.

fields.title: minted_amount
fields.description:
Quantity minted by this registration. Never negative — nothing exists
 to burn yet.

anyOf.title: UpgradeRegistryNode
anyOf.description:
The CIP-113 UPGRADE path for the OTHER logic scripts.

 `registry_spend`'s in-place update branch (the `None` case, when no
 registry NFT is minted) lets a node's `transfer_logic_script`,
 `third_party_transfer_logic_script`, `unfracking_logic_script` and
 `global_state_cs` be rewritten, while `key`, `next` and
 `minting_logic_script` stay frozen forever
 (`is_field_updated_registry_node`). It gates that on
 `pairs.has_key(self.withdrawals, spent_node.minting_logic_script)` —
 i.e. on the permanent proxy, which delegates here. So this validator is
 the sole authority over whether this token's transfer rules may change.

 The base layer already guarantees, for this shape: exactly one registry
 node output (`expect [cont]`), the frozen fields unchanged, and that
 this token's own asset is neither minted nor burned in the same
 transaction (`expect !mint_has_policy(self.mint, spent_node.key)`).
 What it does NOT constrain is our deployment's own invariants — it
 happily lets `global_state_cs` be re-pointed away from our GlobalState
 and `unfracking_logic_script` be switched on — so those are re-asserted
 here.

fields.title: registry_node_input_index
fields.description: Index into `self.inputs` — this token's registry node, being spent.

fields.title: global_state_ref_input_index
fields.description:
Index into `self.reference_inputs` — GlobalState, read for the admin
 credential and the upgrade lock. Referenced rather than spent: no
 supply changes, so there is no cap to enforce.

anyOf.title: RegisterStructural
anyOf.description:
A CIP-113 registration that mints nothing — it only creates the registry
 node. GlobalState is merely REFERENCED (there is no supply change, so
 no cap to enforce and no reason to spend it), and the admin alone
 authorises. Asserting that nothing is in fact minted is what keeps this
 from being a way around `RegisterMint`'s power-user and receiver gates.

fields.title: global_state_ref_input_index
fields.description:
Index into `self.reference_inputs` — GlobalState, read for the admin
 credential.

types/minting_authority/MintingLogicDest.title: MintingLogicDestinationAction
types/minting_authority/MintingLogicDest.description:
One entry per unique destination (unique stake-credential among outputs
 carrying the security token) when minting. Mirrors the transfer-logic
 destination action: a KYC proof (checked only when
 `GlobalStateDatum.requires_receiver_kyc`) and a denylist-absence
 covering-node reference-input index (always checked). CMTAT v3.2.0
 refuses to mint to a frozen address (core) or to a non-allowlisted one
 (Allowlist variant); this is the eUTxO equivalent.

types/minting_logic_script/MintingLogicS.title: MintingLogicScriptWithdrawRedeemer
types/minting_logic_script/MintingLogicS.description:
Withdraw redeemer for minting_logic_script.ak — the permanent,
 CIP-113-registered PROXY.

 The proxy makes exactly one decision: "is the minting authority that
 GlobalState currently names running in this transaction?" It therefore
 needs exactly one thing from the caller — where to find GlobalState. Every
 other decision, and so every other redeemer field, belongs to the
 authority (see types/minting_authority.ak).

 The two constructors exist only because a UTxO cannot be both spent and
 referenced: a mint or burn must SPEND GlobalState (so its `MintSecurity`
 branch runs and enforces the supply cap), while a structural registration
 merely REFERENCES it. The proxy does not care which of those is happening
 — it just needs to read the datum — so it accepts either and leaves the
 "was the right one used for this operation?" judgement to the authority.

types/power_users/PowerUser.title: PowerUser
types/power_users/PowerUser.description:
Power users are the BAFIN protocol's operators. Each flag is independent —
 a power user holds exactly the set of permissions granted to them.

 KYC verification is no longer a power-user concern — it's delegated to
 trusted-entity-issued signed proofs (see `lib/types/kyc_proof.ak`).

 Authority split: power-user *list* lifecycle (add/remove/modify power users)
 is gated by the single GS admin credential. Sanctions (denylist) add/remove
 is delegated to any power user holding `is_admin` + their signature, so a
 compliance role can be granted without handing over the master admin key.

types/third_party_transfer_logic_script/.title: ThirdPartyDestinationAction
types/third_party_transfer_logic_script/.description:
One entry per unique destination (unique stake-credential among outputs
 carrying the security token). Admin provides a KYC proof for each
 destination + a denylist-absence covering-node reference index.

 Source is NOT checked — force transfer is an admin override: the source
 may be denylisted or its KYC may have expired. That's the point.

fields.title: registry_node_ref_input_index
fields.description:
Index into `self.reference_inputs` — the CIP-113 registry node for THIS
 token. See `MintingLogicScriptWithdrawRedeemer` for why it is named
 rather than searched for.

types/transfer_logic_script/TransferLogi.title: TransferLogicScriptAction
types/transfer_logic_script/TransferLogi.description:
One action per unique sender (unique stake-credential among inputs carrying
 the security token). Binds a KYC proof to that sender and a covering-node
 reference-input index proving the sender's pkh is absent from the denylist.

types/transfer_logic_script/TransferLogi.title: TransferLogicScriptDestinationAction
types/transfer_logic_script/TransferLogi.description:
One action per unique destination. Both a fresh KYC proof bound to the
 destination and a denylist-absence proof are required.

 Rationale: Swiss CO Art. 973e (DLT Act) requires the issuer to perform
 obligations only to a named creditor in the ledger; eWpG §14 requires the
 issuer to maintain a register of identified holders; and industry-standard
 regulated-securities designs (ERC-3643; CMTAT with RuleWhitelist) gate
 both sender and recipient. Requiring a destination proof on regular
 transfers matches all three.

types/transfer_logic_script/TransferLogi.title: TransferLogicScriptWithdrawRedeemer
types/transfer_logic_script/TransferLogi.description:
Transfer-logic withdraw redeemer.

 - `global_state_ref_input_index` — GS UTxO as ref input; provides pause
   flag, TEL, denylist policy id.
 - `actions_for_each_input` — one KYC proof + denylist-absence covering-node
   index per unique sender, ordered to match the aggregated-senders order.
 - `destination_actions` — one KYC proof + denylist-absence covering-node
   index per unique destination, ordered to match the aggregated-destinations
   order. Both positive (KYC) and negative (denylist absence) attestations
   required on receive.

fields.title: registry_node_ref_input_index
fields.description:
Index into `self.reference_inputs` — the CIP-113 registry node for THIS
 token. See `MintingLogicScriptWithdrawRedeemer` for why it is named
 rather than searched for.
